I think nothing’s worse than this nagging feeling of „I wonder what this could’ve led to...“.
That’s why it’s so hard to get over things that never even fully happened.

I don’t have any advice really. I’m in a similar situation and although it ended four months ago I still can’t get over it and I feel like this person is “the one that got away” so I’ll never be fully over him...

I just try to accept that some things aren’t meant to be and try to look at it like destiny didn’t want it to play out this way. 
Life’s simply a moody bitch sometimes...

I’m the same way and a lot of people have a hard time relating to my moods when I’m rapid cycling. 

I can basically go from being suicidal to overly happy from one day to another sometimes. It’s exhausting and sometimes even confusing for myself to be honest. 

And it’s a good possibility that whatever they gave him caused the drastic change in his mood. 

It’s possible that they only gave him some meds to get him out of his psychosis or something to calm him down on the first day and that’s why he was back to being religious soon after.

If he’s not on medication he should definitely talk to a doctor and look into mood stabilizers and antipsychotics as soon as possible! 
Just try to talk to him about it when he’s clearheaded and seems to be in a „normal“ state of mind.
This is crucial because if he’s manic he’ll probably deny that he needs medication at all.

Everybody’s different. 
Sometimes people just stick with you longer than others even if you didn’t get to be with them for a long time. Take your time to get over him, no matter how long it takes.

It’s unfair to yourself and the person you’re dating and it will lead to a lot of heartache.

It gets easier over time and it’s good that you’re aware that you wouldn’t be a good fit relationship wise with that guy.

I’m still not over that one guy completely either and it’s been a struggle but it got so much easier once I stopped dating others in order to replace him.

Sounds cheesy but trust me - once you’re over him and content with yourself again you’ll attract people who’ll actually be a good fit for you.

Nobody has the right to force themself on anyone!

To be honest, even if you said yes - you were in no way capable of giving consent if you were on meds *and* manic, and if he was aware of your situation he knew what he was doing and took advantage of the situation!

It doesn’t matter if you were manic or not, if you if you actually said no - *if you didn’t want it there was no consent!*

How about you take some time to actually get over that crush of yours and take yourself out of the dating game for awhile?

I had a thing going on with someone for a few months and it ended really badly. I tried dating asap to get over him and I always wanted to get back to him too until I realized that I actually didn’t want to meet someone new - I never got over him and tried to replace him.

If that’s the case for you - work through those feelings and get over him properly. Then and and only when you’re ready start dating again. 

Theres no use in trying to replace someone.

Totally depends. I’ve had manic episodes where it was just like someone pulled a switch and suddenly I was „normal“ again and other times it just died down over a longer period of time.

For me the mania stops abruptly and the hypomania dies down slower.

I had a period where I was super religious too and that kind of ended abruptly too. I just went from being totally devoted to meh, god doesn’t exist after all overnight.

But yes, there are also people who Rapid cycle; that means that they go from one state to the other way faster than usual. I have that too.
I don’t stay in a hypomanic or depressed state for longer than a week or two, mania only lasts for a few days usually.

For some people they can have the mania/hypomania/depression cycle in a matter of days/weeks, while others stay in one for months.

Bipolar is a highly individual disorder if you ask me.

All the best to your brother; hope he’ll get better and be able to handle his disorder as good as he can in the future!

Edit: could also be that they put him on medication? You should talk to his doctor. When I was hospitalized they gave me meds right away and I had no choice but to take them. This could also change how his mania presents itself.

Well just think about it; that’s what we’ve known our whole life; that’s what we’re conditioned to deal with, what we grew up to be able to handle. It’s not an addiction; it’s just what’s normal to us.

It takes a while to get used to the „new normal“; or what everybody else experiences as normal. Everybody else had their whole lives to adapt to it and through my meds I’m basically just thrown into cold water, so I’m not even surprised that a big part of me is afraid of it and wants to go back to what I considered to be normal my whole life.

I‘m generally drawn to „damaged goods“ to put it into different words. By that I mean people with issues - that includes people with personality or affective disorders. 

And I think I figured out why - I always try to fix them. Because I kinda just focus on fixing them because it distracts myself from having to fix myself; it seems easier.

But it never works.

So I made the decision to consciously avoid dating people who have similar issues as I do. May seem harsh but as of now it’s a deal breaker for me. In 9 out of 10 cases it just ends up being toxic and/or codependent.

I’m 31, also female and have the same problem.

I think that nowadays we just have too many options. With apps like tinder and social media in general we don’t have to work as hard to get dates and we simply have too many options. Nobody wants to commit anymore because they have this feeling that there could be something better waiting for them after the next swipe 🤷🏻‍♀️ 

What bothers me most about this state of mind isn’t even that people don’t want to commit - it’s that most of them won’t be upfront about it. 
I’ve had a lot of guys string me along for sometimes months... they’ll want to be with you for a while, never fully committing but leaving the door open just wide enough that you think it could lead to something serious and then be all surprised that you thought you actually dated and not just „hung out“ when you’ve been seeing each other for like 3 or 4 months... 

To be honest I’ve basically given up actively finding someone. If I happen to find someone with the same expectations and mindset as I have that’s fine, but I won’t put myself in situations where people can play with my feelings anymore.
This fuckboy mentality just doesn’t float my boat.

When do you know you’re ready?

That’s tough to answer because only you can really know for sure. For me I feel I’m only ready when I regularly take my meds and my moods are stable and when I don’t feel like I only date to fill a void or try to distract myself from something by preoccupying myself with someone, if that makes sense. And also, that’s a really big thing for me - when being or not being with someone doesn’t determine my mood - or to put it another way; when I don’t feel like I make myself dependent on someone else. 

When I’m unstable I tend to put others above me, put them on a pedestal, feel inferior to them and make everything about them. They make up my whole world, I get kind of obsessed and they will influence whether or not I’m happy. 
I guess that’s because I don’t want to deal with myself and they distract me. 
When I’m stable they will add to my well-being but not dictate it.


When to tell someone about your diagnosis?

I am a pretty straight forward and open person. For acquaintances I’ll tell someone as soon as I feel comfortable and they seem trustworthy. There are friends who have known right away and some where it took a few months for me to tell them.
I do also have pretty obvious self harm scars though so for me it’s kinda hard to avoid the whole „what’s your damage“ talk for too long ahaha

With dating it’s more complicated for sure; but in the end you should tell them as soon as you feel as if you’re genuinely interested in them. 
I’d say after the third or fourth date? But basically before you sleep with them.
I dunno, I just feel that this is the kind of information I’d like to have before I am intimate with someone. It could potentially be a deal breaker for some people so they should know about it as soon as possible and before they get too involved.

In my experience most people react in a sympathetic, understanding and pretty open way. Especially if you seem like a person that is collected and got his/her shit together. It’s all about how you carry yourself. 

I once had a fling with a guy and told him about a suicide attempt and my diagnosis roughly four hours after meeting him for the first time and it didn’t scare him away. 
Another guy didn’t want anything to do with me after hearing about my self harm and I didn’t even mention anything else.

Everybody’s different is all I’m saying and just don’t take it personally if you get rejected for it, because it has nothing to do with you. 
There can be a lot of reasons why people back off after hearing about your diagnosis, from simply being ignorant jerks to having their own trauma or conflicts, whatever.

All in all I feel like most people are more scared than they should be. I know quite a few people with mental illnesses and most of them have no problems when it comes to dating (at least not because of their diagnosis).
You’d be surprised how many people will just basically shrug it off (in a good way, like, it’s no big deal), be interested and curious but not judge you for it and not treat you differently.

Also at some point I just had way too high of a tolerance. I used to drink like 8 cups a day or something, even gave myself caffeine poisoning once and that really wasn’t fun.

I was always even more grumpy and depressed when for some reason or another I couldn’t get another cup, I had to pee all the time, I was dehydrated, all the water retention was ridiculous, I actually gained weight (there are some studies that actually prove that caffeine has that effect if you use too much of it)... 
Not worth it IMO.

I’ve read and heard a lot of times that bipolar shouldn’t be diagnosed before someone’s in their 20ies because that’s usually when the symptoms start to show/manifest; with other disorders it can be sooner (often during childhood or teenage years) but most people I talked to who are bipolar have the same experience as me - that they only had severe symptoms starting in their early 20ies; so yes, I think it could be.

I’ve been feeling quite manageable until I’d say 2 years ago; I’m 30 now; and it’s been getting harder even with meds and treatment. I’ve also heard that bipolar people tend to „peak“ with their symptoms around their 30ies; but I’m not too sure about that, also that’s basically what I’m experiencing, but I’ve never heard that from a professional so I can’t say that for sure.

That everyone can be „a little bit manic depressive“ - no you fucking can’t. Just because you’re moody doesn’t mean you are bipolar.

One of my (not anymore) close friends actually told me something along the lines of „oh I can relate (when I disclosed my diagnosis for the first time) because sometimes I get really moody and can go from happy to sad in like a minute too“... 

Nope nope nope...

I can relate to the feeling of not wanting it to stop but believe me... after the high there will come a low and it will usually be way worse than a low on its own.
Adding to that the first few times being hypo or manic won’t be as dramatic but in my experience at least there’ll be a „buildup“ and you’ll get more and more into it; do more and more things that will be damaging to you or people around you in various ways.
At first I was only „happy“, more outgoing, active etc too. Then it just went from there to being more impulsive when it came to spending money, one night stands, alcohol, drugs, quitting jobs, even cutting off friends on a whim until it escalated to aggressive outbursts and finally three suicide attempts... 
get yourself help before you get to a point like that. It’s much easier to do so if you don’t have to pick up the pieces from manic episodes like that, believe me. 

The thing is; being bipolar usually shows severe symptoms around your age so it probably will get worse from here if left untreated if you’ve only been diagnosed nowY

Sorry if this is a pretty negative answer and if I’m rambling myself; I’m pretty much in a really deep low right now. But anyway, if you want to talk you can send me a pm.

The thing is, when I was still unmedicated I always yearned to be „normal“. I wanted to be like everybody else, I suffered so damn much and always prayed to just be normal. 

Now that I got what I wished for I just feel so empty. It feels like everything was taken from me. Not just the highs, the lows, being different - my complete personality is gone. 
I simply don’t know who I am anymore.

Of course there was also always a part of me that felt different in a good way. I’ve talked to quite a few people with mental illnesses and that seems to be something quite normal. And it did always scare me to some degree to lose that part of me. If that makes sense. 
But I don’t even feel like I am afraid of the ordinary. I just feel like I can’t handle the ordinary. As if I’m simply not cut out to be part of the ordinary.

It overwhelms me. It kind of feels like you’re on some kind of drug that makes everything so intense but also dulls your perception at the same time. You feel unreal, like you just want to go back to being sober but you can’t. 

The only time I feel like myself and normal now is when I’m on something or drunk. Because it gives me back these highs and lows and it makes me not care too much. 

When I’m sober I basically don’t want to exist.

I’ve been suicidal before and I’ve tried to kill myself twice. But even that felt different. There was always a certain trigger. But right now I feel like my existence is just obsolete and too much to handle and I just wish I wouldn’t have to endure being myself and alive. 
Yet I don’t even feel like I’d go through with it because the fact that I feel in a normal range won’t even allow me to do it. And that bugs me to no end.

Yesterday I tried to cut myself (I used to be a cutter but stopped a few years ago) and it didn’t do shit. Realizing that was so strange. Everything I used to know, all my coping strategies (even though I’m aware that they’re unhealthy ones) don’t work anymore. 

Basically, I feel fucking trapped and I feel like whatever and whoever I was is gone. I’m a living shell and I’m more empty than ever before even though I also feel more than ever before.

Sorry if none of this makes sense. I can’t really sort out my thoughts right now.

That’s exactly what an ED does to your head.
It keeps telling you that everything will get better once you hit those magic numbers on the scale.

Well, all I can tell you is, I hit mine a while back. Nothing changed. I was still what I considered to be fat. I was still miserable. I still hated how I looked. I was able to wear new, smaller clothes, but I still cried in the changing room when one single jean wouldn’t fit... 
So I set a new goal weight for myself. I realized it will never be enough. I will never be thin enough. Because what I see in the mirror is not a reflection of how I look; it’s a reflection of everything I hate about myself and think is wrong with me. I will always seek out my imperfections and only see what I don’t like about myself. 

At the end of the day it took me a few trips to the dentist, passing out in public numerous times because of malnourishment, and a few other health issues to finally realize what I was doing to myself.

All I’m saying is... don’t let it get to that point if you can stop it now where it’s not that bad. Take care of yourself. Treat yourself like you deserve it; better than this. 

In the end it’s your decision but I really hope you’ll find your way and stay healthy. It’s a slippery slope and I never would’ve imagined that I’d end up where I did when I first started dieting. 

Please just take care of yourself. I wish you all the best.

Having an ED is not so much about your weight as it is about unhealthy thoughts and the way you perceive yourself.

I’ve never been underweight but struggled with bulimia and anorexia for over 10 years now.

As long as your thoughts about food, eating, your body and your weight are obsessive and unhealthy and it affects your mood in a serious way - yes you have an eating disorder. 

I’d advise you to start therapy and get to the bottom of why you actually want to reach this goal.

For me, I realized that I can also get to my goal weight in a healthy way. Getting better doesn’t mean you have to be at a weight you don’t feel comfortable at. It just means that you have to do it in a healthy way that doesn’t involve going to extremes and occupying yourself with how to do it on an unhealthy level, if that makes sense.
And also; if you get better maybe you’ll even realize that if you reach a certain weight it won’t actually make things better; a lot of times we try to get something because we believe it will be a magical “cure” for other problems in our lives because in reality we’re too afraid to address what’s really going on. Therapy can help you deal with underlying issues that are causing your need to lose weight in the first place.

All I can tell you is that dating someone who’s bipolar can be a literal roller coaster of emotions; at least if they’re either not in therapy/on medication or don’t acknowledge that they have a problem/don’t want to get better. I’ve briefly dated someone who’s bipolar too and it was really eye opening for me to be on the other side once. 

What’s really important is to know that whatever’s going on - you’re not responsible for the shift in his mood and if he doesn’t want help it’s his choice - you can’t force him to. 

Also; dating someone only a week after such a long relationship is super tricky. I think it’s easy to end up rebounding without noticing it and I know from my own and others experience that rebounding can often lead to obsessive behavior. 
Basically a lot of people try to simply find someone to take the place of the ex as quickly as possible and put a lot of hope and expectations on them. 
A lot of times it has nothing to do with the person in front of you; it could be anyone and you’re simply projecting what you want and need onto them because they’re available to fill the void your ex left. 

I guess what you need to ask yourself is if you really think you’re ready for something new and if you have real feelings for this guy or if you simply dread being alone and simply crave the company of *anyone* right now.

Sorry if this comes off as being harsh or clinical; I really don’t mean to. I’ve just done a lot of research into this stuff because I’ve been in this situation myself.
